question: Does one linear map send a stored latent to the latent of a same-xy +90 degree turn, with held-out residual ratio at most 0.70?
claim: On the F2 seed-0 split, least squares from z to z' on train same-xy +90 pairs has test RMS(Rz - z') / RMS(z' - z) at most 0.70, and that ratio is strictly below the constant +90 displacement.
falsifier: Kill if the test ratio is at least 0.90. A computed ratio between 0.70 and 0.90, or a ratio that does not beat the constant displacement, weakens. If fewer than 30 train pairs survive the 5 px and 20 degree gates, the ratio is not computed.
ratio: sqrt(mean(residual^2)) / sqrt(mean((z' - z)^2)) over matrix elements, the F3 ratio
degenerate_check: A 192 by 192 map can memorize a few dozen train pairs. The scored number is the held-out ratio. The constant +90 displacement is the trivial map; support requires the matrix ratio to be strictly smaller. K2 stays closed: this is not a command-only vector on all three turns.

next_action.deepen: The same least-squares matrix on same-xy -90 degree pairs only. One command. Write that falsifier before the fit. Do not fit +180 in that cycle.
next_action.pivot: The +90 matrix claim is withdrawn. Do not add a nonlinear map. The next cycle frames B7 on the Xeon.
next_action.kill: Archive the +90 matrix on this table. The next cycle frames B7 on the Xeon. Do not relax the 5 px or 20 degree gate.
next_action.escalate: Stop. Do not rent a GPU.
